Reel Studio

One tool that does it all. Type a topic — or tap a day from your 30-day library — and it writes the hook, the script, the caption and the hashtags for you, then finds photos and video clips that match the topic itself and renders the finished video right here in your browser, vertical for reels or wide for YouTube, as a real file you can download and post. No uploads needed, no accounts.

  1. 1 Pick a topic or a library day
  2. 2 Auto-generate — or write your own
  3. 3 Preview & tweak
  4. 4 Render & download the video

✦ Auto mode — topic in, finished reel out

Pick a niche and a viral format, type any topic — or tap a day from your 30-day calendar below — and Reel Studio writes the hook, the scene-by-scene script, the caption and the hashtags for you, then searches Wikimedia Commons for a photo or video clip that matches each scene's own words — videos first — and renders the finished video: one click, done. Library days load ready to preview instead, so you can tweak before rendering. Every reel is built hook-first, with a save/CTA ending and a loop back to the hook.

1 Script

One line = one scene. The first line is your hook — make it stop the scroll. Long lines are split into scenes automatically. Auto mode above writes this whole box for you; edit anything you like before rendering.

2 Scenes

Fine-tune each scene: edit the words, set its seconds, or give it its own photo or video clip. Auto mode fills every scene with topic-matched media from Wikimedia Commons — use 🔍 Find on a scene to search and pick a different one yourself, or ⟳ to re-roll that scene's media. Leave a scene empty and the background below is used.

Find media

Free photos & videos from Wikimedia Commons. Tap one to put it on the scene.

3 Backgrounds

Mix mode is on: scenes rotate through the pack.
Clips play as moving backgrounds behind the captions and loop to fill every scene. You can also drag & drop video or photo files straight onto any scene in the list above.

The pack and the four ▶ animated backgrounds above (Particles, Waves, Light streaks, Pulse rings) are the fallback now — used only for scenes where no topic media was found and you added none of your own. The animated ones are real motion too: they render into the exported video, not just the preview.

With a key, topic media comes from Pexels first and Wikimedia Commons is the fallback. Without one, everything works keyless via Commons. The key stays in this browser and is sent only to api.pexels.com.

4 Voiceover

Every reel gets a voice. The voiceover script below is the full narration — longer than the short on-screen captions. Generate it free with your browser's built-in voice, upload an audio file, or record with your microphone. Auto-time scenes then stretches the scenes to match the voice, and the voice is mixed into the exported video.

Making it post-ready

  • Auto mode: every generated reel is hook-first, ends with a save/follow CTA, and loops back to the hook — the three things that keep people watching and rewatching.
  • Format: step 7 switches between Reel (9:16, for Instagram, TikTok and Shorts) and YouTube (16:9 wide). The recorded file type depends on your browser: Chrome, Edge and Firefox record WebM, Safari records MP4. After any render you can also tap “Also download as MP4” for a free in-browser conversion — best for Instagram's uploader. If a recording ever comes out empty, the renderer automatically retries once in the other format before giving you the download.
  • Length: anything from 15 seconds to 10 minutes. Rendering is real time, so a 10-minute video takes about 10 minutes and makes a big file; HD quality keeps long videos lighter.
  • Sync: upload your voiceover first, then hit Auto-time scenes so captions land with the narration.
  • Pace: 2–4 seconds per scene keeps people watching; hooks work best under 8 words.
  • Topic media: Auto mode searches Wikimedia Commons per scene and prefers video; swap any scene with 🔍 Find, re-roll it with ⟳, or drop your own clip on it — yours always wins.
  • Credits: Commons photos and clips are free to use, and many ask for a credit line — the ready-made credits list under the hashtag pack is built from the media actually in your reel; paste it into your post.
  • Video & voice: drop real clips onto scenes (or upload them in step 3) for moving backgrounds, and generate the free browser voiceover in step 4 — it is recorded into the exported video and the scenes re-time themselves to it.
